title: Proofs and Concepts: The Fundamentals of Abstract Mathematics
author: Dave Witte Morris and Joy Morris, incorporating material by P. D. Magnus
note: A bridge course connecting elementary logic with sets, functions, equivalence relations, induction and cardinality.
use: Practice complete arguments before entering proof-based algebra and analysis.

title: An Introduction to Proofs and the Mathematical Vernacular
author: Martin V. Day
note: Uses number systems, polynomials and determinants to practise reading and constructing longer mathematical arguments.
use: Bridge computational courses to upper-level mathematical writing.
accessNote: Author's Virginia Tech page provides the full 147-page book, CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 US.

author: H. Jerome Keisler
version: Online edition 2007; author calculus page identifies update June 2022

title: Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms
author: Per-Gunnar Martinsson and Joel A. Tropp
note: A substantial survey connecting random embeddings and matrix sampling to least squares, low-rank approximation and linear solvers.
prerequisites: Linear algebra, numerical matrix methods and elementary probability.
use: Bridge a numerical linear algebra course to randomized algorithms and their analysis.

title: The Calculus of Functions of Several Variables
author: Dan Sloughter
note: Develops multivariable differentiation as affine approximation, then integration, change of variables, line integrals and Green's theorem.
use: Study geometric explanations alongside a multivariable calculus course.

author: Dan Sloughter

prerequisites: Algebra and trigonometry; prior exposure to calculus is helpful.
use: Revisit calculus through an infinitesimal formulation.

title: Elementary Number Theory
author: W. Edwin Clark; revised by Jim Hefferon
version: Hefferon revision December 2003; PDF compiled January 5, 2004
note: Develops divisibility, prime numbers, congruences, arithmetic functions, primality tests and public-key cryptography through short theorem-based chapters.
prerequisites: School algebra; basic sets and functions. Calculus I is suggested in the preface, chiefly for mathematical maturity.
use: Build proof-writing skill while learning elementary arithmetic theory.

use: Bridge concrete limits to metric-space arguments through the accompanying exercises.
